prize_parts.citation: for showing how technological change and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wage structure and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My laureate set and ballot are unchanged from round 1, but my reasoning is narrower. B006 still meets the common criteria best: a well-posed causal question, a conceptual account of how technology shifts relative labour demand, and transparent local-labour-market designs for import competition. The skill-premium work is about three decades old, the task framework over two decades, and the trade-shock papers more than a decade. They have been replicated across countries and periods and have shaped trade, political economy and macro as well as labour. On the chair's question about shift-share inference and persistence, I think the committee does not need to settle the long-run magnitude. What is established is that exposure to import competition lowered local labour demand and that adjustment was slow and uneven. The size of the effects and their duration remain debated. The citation should claim only the established part. I read the work as one discovery: how exposure to technology and trade shifts labour demand and where the adjustment costs fall. The skill-demand account supplies the interpretive frame and the trade-shock designs supply the identification. I keep Katz for that frame. I do not claim to have settled the Katz-versus-Dorn question, and I would accept Autor, Dorn and Hanson if colleagues show that Katz's marginal credit, once the Goldin work is set aside, is thin. This is a judgement call, and I have not tried to make it look settled. The citation avoids claiming origin of the task framework, so Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu are not misattributed. It also does not restate the 2023 (women's labour-market outcomes) or 2024 (institutions and prosperity) citations. My configuration did not move after the exchange. I tested it against the Dorn variant, the two-name Autor-Hanson set and B007, and found no argument that outweighed B006's identification, breadth and confirmation record.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest point. Dorn is a central co-author of the China-shock papers and is excluded only by the three-person cap. Katz's best-known education-technology work was with Goldin, so his marginal claim is the most exposed in the trio. The task framework has contributors outside the credited set. It is also arguable that technology and trade are two discoveries joined by a common outcome, which would make the citation a composite. The persistence and magnitude of China-shock effects, and shift-share inference, are unresolved. If the committee reads attribution as disqualifying, B007 has the cleaner credit, though with weaker identification and a closer thematic link to the 2024 prize. B004 is influential and mature, but any trio from its eight names leaves out major contributors.

responses.point: Friberg prefers B007 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) for its comparatively clean credit and breadth. He treats B006 as two related lines and would credit only Autor and Hanson, because Katz's work with Goldin sits beside a prize already given.
responses.response: I agree with Friberg on B007's attribution and maturity, and I agree that the 2024 prize rested on a different empirical agenda from the electoral-rule and constitutional programme. Where I differ is identification. Cross-country effects of regimes and rules are hard to separate from confounders. That is a point I know from work on democratisation, so I hold B007 to that standard and do not give it a pass for being near my own field. For me to prefer B007 I would need to see evidence on electoral-rule and constitutional effects that holds up under quasi-experimental or historical identification, and a statement of what it adds beyond the 2024 prize. I do not think the cleaner credit line is outweighed by a scientific disagreement alone, but it does not outweigh B006's stronger identification. On the two-name set, I see the Autor-Hanson pair as coherent. But it reduces the achievement to the trade and task evidence and drops the skill-demand account of why the shocks matter for wages. I would take Dorn over a pair before I would drop the third name.

responses.point: Strömberg names Katz's claim as the most exposed part of the trio, because of his education-technology work with a recent laureate. He says Autor, Dorn and Hanson would be the natural fallback within the same discovery.
responses.response: I agree that Katz's claim is the most exposed, and my round-1 file called it the closest call. I would handle it through the citation, not the name list. It should rest on the wage-structure and skill-demand framework, which is distinct from the education-race work with Goldin. If the committee cannot word it that way without restating the 2023 prize, then the Autor-Dorn-Hanson fallback is the right one. I would call that a drafting test and not a merit question. My reading is that the drafting works. The wording 'wage structure and local labour-market adjustment' avoids the gender and long-run history themes that the 2023 prize covered.

responses.point: Hassler keeps Katz because the skill-premium line makes the trade evidence interpretable. He would accept Dorn for Katz if the committee decides the trade-shock evidence is the core. He also says the citation must avoid ground already covered by the 2023 and 2024 prizes.
responses.response: I share both conditions. Katz stays if the committee decides the achievement is the combined account of technology and trade acting on labour demand. Dorn replaces Katz if the committee prefers the trade-shock design as the core. I do not think the committee needs both formulations to be equally strong. It needs to choose the one that fits how it describes the discovery. On adjacency, I agree with your point that a contested magnitude is not an unconfirmed finding. I would add that adjacency to other prizes bears on timing and framing, not on merit. We should still state in the committee's reasoning what B006 adds beyond the 2023 and 2024 prizes. That is the local-labour-market evidence on trade exposure and the empirical account of skill demand.

responses.point: Krusell moved from B007 to B006 and keeps Katz over Dorn. He argues that dropping Katz would narrow the citation to the trade-shock evidence. He keeps B007 as his first alternative and discloses a proximity to Persson.
responses.response: I agree that dropping Katz narrows the citation to the trade-shock design. That is the real trade-off, not a question of whose contribution is larger. Krusell's remark that the shared support counts for nothing is right, and I treat the tally the same way, since agreement among ten members tells us about convergence and not merit. I would keep B007 in play as an alternative, with the same caveat as above about identification. I also note his disclosure about Persson, and I do not adjudicate it.

responses.point: Andersson moved from B004 first to B006. He argues that one citation can hold both strands, because both concern how exposure to technology and trade shifts labour demand and distributes adjustment costs, and he accepts that B004 attribution is a real weakness.
responses.response: I agree that one citation can hold both strands if it is framed around labour-demand adjustment. That answers the chair's one-discovery-or-two question for me. It also confirms my round-1 concern about B004: I ranked it second, and the attribution problem is why it stays an alternative. The framework is mature and influential, but any trio omits Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, who built the estimated versions. I would reconsider B004 only if a narrower pricing-and-policy-rule citation could be drafted without overclaiming credit.

uncertainties: Whether Katz or Dorn is the better third name. This depends on whether Katz's skill-demand contribution can be worded apart from the Goldin work, and on whether the committee frames the achievement as technology and trade together or as the trade-shock design alone.
Whether the committee treats technology and trade as one discovery or two. If it treats them as two, the citation would be a composite and the case for a narrower set would strengthen.
The long-run persistence and magnitude of China-shock effects, the shift-share inference concerns, and whether results generalise beyond the US episode.
How far adjacency to the 2023 and 2024 prizes should weigh on timing despite distinct citations.

Whether B007's electoral-rule and constitutional evidence meets modern identification standards. My reading is based on my own expertise in a neighbouring field, which also makes me cautious about how I weigh it.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is apparent from my supplied profile. My field is political science. B007, my first alternative, is close to my research on institutions and state capacity, and I disclose that proximity without adjudicating it. I hold it to the same identification standard as other fields and do not prefer it. I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of committee members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart. The profile shows no tie to any credited candidate on the shortlist.
